newsitem.title: USA: U.S. hopeful of "open skies' air pact with Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: U.S. hopeful of "open skies' air pact with Taiwan.

text.p: The United States and Taiwan opened negotiations Wednesday on a free market aviation agreement, with a U.S. official saying he hoped an accord could be reached at the end of the two-day round of talks.

The accord would be the second "open skies" aviation agreement reached between the United States and an Asian nation this year. On Jan. 22, the United States reached a free market accord with Singapore.
A Transportation Department spokesman noted that previous rounds had been held with Taiwan in past months and said, "We are hopeful of reaching an agreement this round."
The spokesman, William Mosley, said the pact with Taiwan would be similar to the standard open skies accords that the United States was seeking with Asian and European nations.
It would allow U.S. and Taiwanese carriers to fly to any city they wish and as frequently as they wish, with the added right to fly beyond those cites to third countries.
The United States is also seeking open skies pacts with Malaysia, South Korea and New Zealand. It has free market accords with 12 European countries.

Open skies talks with Japan are set for Washington next week, but, signalling an agreement with Tokyo is not near, a department official characterised them not as "negotiations" but as "senior level meetings."
